title: Tell the Robot What You Want — Sandhya Subramani, AWS
talk_summary: A demo-heavy AWS talk showing a Strands Agents harness layered on a small rover, where an LLM agent selects among pre-programmed robot policies/tools from natural-language commands. The architecture separates an agent layer (decides what) from a policy layer (decides how), with cloud/edge split for training vs runtime execution.

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent layer only chooses which pre-trained policy/tool to invoke; the policy layer owns execution mechanics, so the LLM never has to reason about low-level control.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent decides what to do and the policy decides how it should be done

takeaways.technique: Multiple concurrent specialized agents on one shared body
takeaways.what_they_do: Three Strands agents run simultaneously: a continuously-thinking 'thinker', a communication agent (Telegram/web), and a voice agent, each with a distinct role over the same underlying tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: He's got three different agents. All three of them are strands and all three of them are working simultaneously.

takeaways.technique: Enumerate tools with per-tool purpose in system prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: The system prompt lists every available tool and explicitly states what each is meant for, which the agent uses to pick the right tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm telling it what each of these rules are meant for. And so that's how strand decides which tool to invoke

takeaways.technique: Use the agent to generate its own training/eval episodes
takeaways.what_they_do: They manually drive the robot and log its reasoning per command to build training episodes and improve behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can use him to create my data sets because I'm able to also manually move him
